AMENDMENT (pre-grill, from the adversarial review of the idea set — a fresh pi review run read-only against the five contracts). Three changes to this contract:
(1) THE FINDINGS SHAPE LOSES PROVENANCE. AC-2's {id, severity, where, text, status} has no recorder — but the precedent it copies, evidence.answers[] {id, answer, provenance}, HAS it, and design v3 §6 + AGENTS.md require inference to be labelled as inference. A finding whose author is unknown is indistinguishable from a human's. AMEND AC-2: each finding carries provenance (the model/provider when a session produced it, the human when a person did).
(2) AC-5 CANNOT FAIL. 'A MISS is recorded as a finding about the CONTEXT, never hidden' means no outcome is a failure — the one experiment that could falsify this task (and 12/11's read, and the held journey-session) has no threshold. AMEND AC-5: the oracle run is RECORDED as evidence on the node with a stated minimum — the three code-visible prior findings (F4 handlers.ts:433 · G1 approve.ts:212 · G5 ui-drill.test.ts:436) — and a MISS blocks the confirm gate by NAME (the F-AC18 refusal shape), so the packet gap it exposes is itself the finding rather than a green run.
(3) THE WHY'S TRANSPORT. This task's AC-4 forbids writing a gate event (correct), yet 12/11 AC-1 requires the human's why ON the gate decision and its oracle wants the session to END with that why on the record. Nothing transports it today, so the session would end in the human retyping a sentence. AMEND: the session DRAFTS the why as a proposal (recorded as drafted-not-confirmed); the human's gate gesture records it. No new write path, no session-written gate event — the transport is the human's own decision, pre-filled.
ALSO RECORDED: 12/09 owns the FIFTH profile (review at the confirm gate). Any journey-scope session is a SIXTH and is HELD, not spawned — see the review's finding that its records have no legal home yet (a journey-scope session has no node; openQuestions live in an immutable node.json; the session may not write a gate event; .ann/ideas/ does not exist yet). 12/10 + 12/11 are its prerequisites.

 · F4 — src/surface/handlers.ts IS NOT IN THE RANGE AT ALL (`git diff --name-only <range>` over that path is empty; the file was never touched by the delivery). A material built from the DELIVERY's patch cannot show a pre-existing defect in a file the delivery did not touch, whatever the budget. This is structural, and it is the more important of the two.
 · G1 and G5 — both files ARE in the range and both were cut: the delivered budget is 60,000 chars and the patch is 137,547 chars, so 77,547 chars are cut. Whether a given file's hunks survive is a function of git's PATH ORDER, not of relevance. The session said so itself, in its own words: "the diff cuts the file at 77,547 chars".

WHAT IT DID VERIFY — 7 findings at `matches`, each from the bytes, each with a file:line:
 F7 src/commands/index.ts:1518 — the command-layer readers delegate to gateView (undecidedSubmission, gateState, rejections, pendingGatesOf, lookBack, frontmostReady, advance); the raw triple scan is gone from that file.

And 6 honest `uncertain` findings naming EXACTLY which bytes were missing and what would settle each — the behaviour this record exists to make possible. Plus one `gap` it raised on its own initiative: the checks are REPORTED claims covering 9 files of 27 changed, which does not meet AC-6's bar.

THE TWO CONTEXT DEFECTS, AS FINDINGS ABOUT THE CONTEXT (AC-5: never hidden):
 1 · THE PATCH IS NOT THE TREE. A delivery's diff cannot show a defect in code the delivery did not change, so a review whose material is the patch alone is structurally blind to exactly the class of defect 12/08 was rejected for (a pre-existing readers sweep). Cause: the material carries `git diff <range>` and nothing else readable. Follow-up owed: a retrieval ability — let the session read a NAMED path at the anchor sha — which is what AC-5's "the inputs are sufficient" ultimately requires and what no bounded single-shot prompt can substitute for.
 2 · THE BOUNDED PATCH IS ORDERED BY PATH, NOT RELEVANCE. With the budget this task ships (60,000 chars) the cut lands wherever the alphabet puts the 137,547-char mark. Cause: one cap over one concatenation. Follow-up owed, if the record shows it matters: per-contract-targetAreas or per-file ordering.

WHAT THIS TASK DID ABOUT EACH, MEASURED. Before the oracle, the budget was 12,000 chars and the session came back `uncertain` on EVERY criterion with 0 findings at `matches` — 8.7% of the patch is not a review. Landed from that measurement: DIFF_CHARS 12,000 -> 60,000; a new `submission.changedFiles` input carrying the COMPLETE change map so a file whose hunks were cut is always NAMED rather than invisible; and the patch now excludes `.ann/journey` (repo-root-anchored, and DISCLOSED in the input text) because the record's own churn sorted first and ate the whole budget. The oracle after those changes verified 7 criteria from the bytes where the first run verified none. Defect 1 is NOT fixed and cannot be by a budget: it is recorded here as owed.

THE AMENDMENT'S 'BLOCKS THE CONFIRM GATE BY NAME' CLAUSE. Recorded as an unresolved TENSION rather than quietly satisfied: this node's own AC-4 forbids the session writing any gate event (a review must never accept, reject or close), so the session cannot BLOCK anything mechanically — and the amendment's other half asks for exactly that. Disposition taken: the MISS is recorded by THE NAME OF ITS CAUSE (above), in a record the gate read exposes per finding, and the human's own gesture at the gate decides. If the operator wants a mechanical block, it belongs to the gate reader (a review with an unreproduced stated minimum shown as a named blocker at `ann confirm`), which is a read-path change, not a session one — and not in this task's declared outputs.

THE ORACLE'S RECORD, COMPLETE. The previous event recorded the run and the 7 criteria it verified FROM THE BYTES; this carries ALL 14 findings it landed, verbatim (id · severity · where · status, then its text as written), because a partial list of a review's findings is the exact shape of record this task exists to replace. note: 12/09 — the review session and the findings record it lands: a review at a gate now produces a RECORD, per finding, on the addressed node, through the one writer, read by the one derivation (commit 4e5c159). The AC-5 oracle ran for real and its outcome, including the MISS and its two measured causes, is on this node.

claims.statement: REVIEW IS A PROFILE, NOT A SECOND SESSION. `REVIEW_PROFILE` is the FOURTH `GrillProfile` (src/flow/review-session.ts) injected into the UNCHANGED core: the round loop, the anti-runaway ceiling, dedupe/never-re-ask, the synthesis turn, `InteractAbort` and provider fail-closed are all src/flow/grill-session.ts's own and are reused, not re-implemented. The one core addition is the optional `GrillProfile.findings` + `GrillOptions.onFindings` hook: ONE extra strict-JSON findings turn per round, and a no-op for a profile that does not declare it — the three existing areas' tests pass UNCHANGED (the proof it is additive) and a new test pins 1 model call per clean round without the hook against 2 with it. Wired at a task's CONFIRM gate by `ann review!`, whose gate is DERIVED from the node (`detail(id).next`), never guessed: it refuses `not-at-confirm-gate` naming the verdict actually in hand, refuses a LEG by name, refuses JSON up-front (`review-interactive`), and refuses a read-only target (it is in JOURNEY_REFUSED_WRITES).

THE FINDINGS ARE A RECORD. Each finding is `{id, severity ∈ matches|gap|regression|quality|uncertain, where (file:line), text, status, provenance}` and rides the EXISTING `evidence` field whitelist, so it lands through the one writer (`Store.appendEvent` → `validateEventShape`), which mints its one target — confinement to the ADDRESSED node is STRUCTURAL, not a check, and asserted: the sibling holds nothing and `verify()` is clean. No hand-written file, no write outside the addressed node, no new write path. The AREA stamps `provenance` and PICKS the five fields, so a model can neither author a finding nor smuggle a key (a forged `provenance` and a `basis` key are dropped; a bad severity reaches the writer and is refused BY NAME). DERIVED-READABLE: `ann confirm`/`detail`/`brief --json` expose the record per finding through ONE derivation `Commands.reviewFindings(id)`, and `Store.detail()` is untouched — it stays lean and re-derives nothing.

PER FINDING, AND THE FLIP IS CHECKABLE. The gate read prints each finding's `id · severity · status · where` plus its text — never a digest, which the tests pin by asserting the per-finding rows, not a summary. A finding's identity is its `id` and the LATEST landing wins, so a subsequent rework/re-review marks each finding `resolved|open` on the next pass; a finding the latest pass did NOT re-state is marked `· NOT RE-ASSESSED by the latest pass` rather than silently dropped — the exact way 12/08's findings were lost. Proof: a fixture whose finding flips only with evidence (a second pass re-stating F1 as resolved supersedes it to pass 2 while an omitted F2 stays at pass 1, stale), plus the no-review case reading honestly as `no review has landed`. A mutation of that per-finding line kills exactly the two tests that assert it; restored byte-identical.

BOUNDED, HONEST, AND IT DECIDES NOTHING. A full session writes NO gate event — asserted by reading the node's events before and after (only `evidence` is appended; `submitted|confirmed|rejected` stay composite-owned by `gate!`), so a review can never accept, reject or close the task it reviewed. Findings land AS ASSERTED after every round through the awaited hook, so a session that dies mid-way has already landed everything it found (a dead provider on round 2's findings turn fails closed with `provider-unavailable` and round 1's finding is already on the node). The rounds are bounded by the core's ceiling (`maxRounds: 1` + refine → `exhausted`, the record intact). A skipped review lands nothing. On a REFUSED landing the session fails closed rather than reporting success.

THE INPUTS ARE PROVEN, AND THE ORACLE IS MEASURED AND RECORDED. Deterministic: unit tests assert the material CONTAINS the contract + its ACs as constraints, the submission's commits, the RANGE they were made over (derived — the log records commits, never the base — and pinned against a REAL node: 12/08's range resolves to the same `a59bf00..b54b67a` its own review was read over, where the naive rule is one commit short), the complete change map, the patch, the captured checks at their sha marked FACT vs CLAIM, the resolved defining docs, and any prior findings. Measured: the session was RUN for real (real provider, one round) against a fixture node carrying 12/08's own contract and its real cited commits, standing at its confirm gate; the outcome is RECORDED on this node in full, per finding, not as a digest. It reproduced 0 of the 3 findings AC-5 names as its stated minimum, with two measured causes recorded: a patch cannot show a defect in a file the delivery never touched (12/08's F4 sits in src/surface/handlers.ts, which the range never changed), and path order — not relevance — decides what a bounded patch keeps. Both are recorded as findings about the CONTEXT and as owed follow-ups (a retrieval ability), never hidden. Landed FROM that measurement: the patch budget 12,000 → 60,000 chars (8.7% of a real delivery is not a review), the complete change map so a cut file is still NAMED, and the record's own churn excluded from the patch and DISCLOSED in the input. After those, the same session verified 7 criteria from the bytes at file:line where the first run verified none. The amendment's 'blocks the confirm gate by name' clause is recorded as an unresolved tension with this node's own AC-4 (the session may not write a gate event), with the disposition taken: the MISS is named by cause in a record the gate read exposes per finding, and the human's gesture decides.

NO REGRESSION, AND THE JOURNEY IS HONEST AT THE DELIVERED SHA. Full `npm test` green (47 files · 946 tests), `npm run typecheck` clean, and the four checks captured by `capture!` at the delivered commit — npm test, npm run typecheck, ann check, ann verify — all PASS, all bound to 4e5c159. `ann check` reports no gate gaps and `ann verify` reports 0 drifts, so the log and the filesystem agree. The README command table stays byte-aligned with `ann commands` (a `review!` row added in both, pinned by the parity test), and the served page carries the record: the UI card renders the findings per finding from the same assembled `brief.findings` the terminal prints, verified over HTTP against a live server.
